stories.title: Replace road-adjacency power with laid-wire connectivity
stories.i_want: a building to be powered only when a wire I laid connects it to a producer with spare capacity
stories.so_that: power exists only where a wire runs, matching the project's one physical-causality rule

acceptance_criteria.text: A building adjacent to a powered road but with no wire hop laid to it is unpowered, even though today's ElectricityCache union-find would mark it powered. [SUBSTRATE: CONFLICTS — map/electricity_cache.rs:39-63,244-280]

Power reachability is computed over an explicit wire-hop graph the planner builds, not over road-graph adjacency; a producer connected only by road (no wire) supplies no one. [SUBSTRATE: CONFLICTS — map/electricity_cache.rs:244-280 (map_electricity_edges)]

A building wired to a producer whose network has no blackout still loses power if the specific wire path to it is capacity-saturated, i.e. blackout is not merely binary per-network as today. [SUBSTRATE: CONFLICTS — map_dynamic/electricity.rs:89]

stories.title: Two-tier voltage transmission with transformers and substations
stories.i_want: a typed chain of plant to HIGH transmission lines to transformer to LOW distribution lines to substation to buildings
stories.so_that: the grid has real topology instead of a flat conductivity brush

acceptance_criteria.text: HIGH-tier lines connect only to plants, transformers, and other HIGH lines; LOW-tier lines connect only to transformers, substations, and buildings — a building cannot draw directly from a HIGH line. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, no voltage-tier concept exists in map/electricity_cache.rs]

A transformer converts HIGH input to LOW output up to its own capacity; drawing more than the transformer's capacity through it leaves downstream substations under-supplied even if upstream plant capacity is ample. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield]

stories.title: Capacitated lines with distance-based transmission loss
stories.i_want: each line class to have a throughput rating and per-km loss, with HIGH lines losing less than LOW
stories.so_that: plant siting and substation placement are physically meaningful decisions

acceptance_criteria.text: A wire segment carrying load above its rated capacity delivers no more than its capacity downstream, regardless of upstream supply. [SUBSTRATE: OURS/ABSENT — greenfield, no $CAPACITY equivalent exists on any Egregoria edge type]

Power delivered at the far end of a LOW line is less than power injected at the near end by an amount proportional to line length, and the same length of HIGH line loses proportionally less. [SUBSTRATE: OURS/ABSENT — greenfield]

stories.title: Priority-class brownout before blackout
stories.i_want: a starved subnetwork to shed load by planner-set priority class (hospitals before housing before industry) with graded brownout before any consumer goes fully dark
stories.so_that: scarcity is felt as leaner tranches, not an unqualified binary outage

acceptance_criteria.text: When a subnetwork's supply falls short of total demand, a lower-priority consumer's draw is reduced (brownout) before a higher-priority consumer loses any power, replacing today's single per-network blackout boolean that treats every consumer identically. [SUBSTRATE: CONFLICTS — map_dynamic/electricity.rs:89 (binary per-network blackout, no priority classes)]

A consumer only goes to full blackout after brownout has already reduced its draw to a floor and supply is still insufficient — blackout is never the first response to a deficit. [SUBSTRATE: CONFLICTS — map_dynamic/electricity.rs:89]

stories.title: Power plants are ordinary recipe buildings
stories.i_want: a power plant to require fuel and workers like any production building, producing electricity only while both are supplied
stories.so_that: generation obeys the same production model as every other recipe building

acceptance_criteria.text: A power plant with no fuel input or no assigned workers produces zero electricity, using the same recipe/backpressure machinery as goods buildings (power_production/power_consumption fields). [SUBSTRATE: PROVIDED pattern — prototypes/src/prototypes/building.rs:34-35, souls/goods_company.rs:36-39]

stories.title: Water sourced, treated, and piped with a quality grade
stories.i_want: water to flow from a source through treatment and pipes to consumers, carrying a 0-1 quality value end to end
stories.so_that: shortage and contamination propagate as unmet need, not a coverage toggle

acceptance_criteria.text: A water source has an output rate and source quality; a treatment plant consumes dirty water plus chemicals plus power and outputs water capped at quality 0.99. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, zero water-system footprint in simulation/src per keyword sweep]
Quality degrades through use and pipe transport is tracked per flow, not reset to a fixed value at each hop. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield]

A sensitive consumer with a declared required quality is gated: it receives no usable water input if delivered quality is below its own class threshold, even though flow rate is sufficient — an animal farm gates below 0.93, a food factory below 0.97, and nuclear cooling below 0.60, so different consumer classes gate at different numeric thresholds, not one shared cutoff. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, thresholds sourced from research/utilities.md §D2]

The water network includes reservoirs/switches as in-line storage and junction hardware, distinct from substations acting as leaf buffers — a reservoir smooths a temporary supply/demand mismatch by drawing down its stored volume instead of immediately failing delivery downstream. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield]

stories.title: Pipe network with capacity and pump-hop loss
stories.i_want: water pipes to have throughput capacity and pumps that push water over distance
stories.so_that: network topology and pump placement are real engineering decisions

acceptance_criteria.text: A pipe segment carrying flow above its capacity delivers no more than its capacity downstream. [SUBSTRATE: OURS/ABSENT — greenfield, no $CAPACITY token in W&R source data either]

stories.title: Water tanker as off-grid delivery
stories.i_want: a building not connected to the pipe network to instead be served by a water tanker truck via the logistics dispatcher
stories.so_that: water reaches buildings the pipe grid hasn't reached yet, at a real logistics cost

acceptance_criteria.text: Water is registered as an ItemID so a truck can carry it as ordinary cargo between a water station and an off-grid building's local buffer. [SUBSTRATE: PARTIAL — item registration substrate exists (prototypes/src/prototypes/item.rs:8-12) but no water dispatch office or truck cargo type is wired up]

An off-grid building fed by tanker shows the same shortage/queue behaviour under insufficient truck capacity as a pipe-fed building shows under insufficient pipe capacity — no special-cased unlimited truck supply. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, depends on the logistics dispatcher (spec/logistics.md) which the audit could not confirm as a generic reusable abstraction]

stories.title: Sewage produced wherever water is consumed
stories.epic_theme: Sewage — the return half of the water cycle
stories.i_want: sewage to accumulate as a byproduct of household water use and as a declared industrial output
stories.so_that: sewage volume is a physical consequence of water consumption, not an independent input

acceptance_criteria.text: A household consuming water produces a corresponding sewage quantity into its local buffer; an industrial recipe building can also declare a fixed sewage output rate independent of water use. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, zero sewage-system footprint per keyword sweep]

stories.title: Sewage network with treat-or-discharge choice
stories.epic_theme: Sewage — the return half of the water cycle
stories.i_want: a pipe network separate from the water network, carrying sewage to either a treatment plant (recovers water at quality 0.85, costs chemicals+power+workers) or a free discharge point (pollutes)
stories.so_that: cheap-now-vs-clean-later is a real planning decision with physical consequences

acceptance_criteria.text: Sewage pipes and water pipes are distinct graphs; a building connected only to the water network cannot route sewage anywhere without a separate sewage pipe connection. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; CONFLICTS with the CS1 shared-grid approach the substrate audit already rejected for electricity]

Routing sewage to a treatment plant instead of a discharge point costs chemicals and power and produces usable water capped at quality 0.85 (lower than fresh treatment's 0.99 ceiling), so recovered water never substitutes for fresh water at food-grade thresholds. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield]

Routing sewage to a discharge point instead requires no chemical/power input but emits pollution into the shared environment model at the discharge location. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, depends on a shared pollution model not yet specified]

stories.title: Sewage overflow backs up and gates water use
stories.epic_theme: Sewage — the return half of the water cycle
stories.i_want: sewage that exceeds treatment/discharge capacity to back up to the nearest discharge point, or, absent one, fill producers' local buffers and stop their water consumption
stories.so_that: a blocked drain physically stops the tap rather than sewage vanishing

acceptance_criteria.text: When treatment capacity is exceeded and a discharge point exists on the network, excess sewage routes there automatically (auto-pollute) instead of being silently dropped. [SUBSTRATE: OURS/ABSENT — greenfield, declared Gaps in both source games]
When no discharge point exists and local sewage buffers fill, the producing building's water consumption is gated (blocked) until buffer space frees up. [SUBSTRATE: OURS/ABSENT — greenfield]

stories.title: Heat plants burn fuel into district heat
stories.epic_theme: Heating — district network with temperature-driven demand
stories.i_want: a heat plant to consume coal and workers and produce heat as an ordinary recipe building, with waste incineration as an alternate fuel source
stories.so_that: heat generation obeys the same production model as electricity and follows the waste-to-heat coupling

acceptance_criteria.text: A heat plant with no coal input or no assigned workers produces zero heat, using the standard recipe/backpressure machinery. [SUBSTRATE: PROVIDED pattern, ABSENT instance — recipe mechanics exist (souls/goods_company.rs:36-39) but no heat plant prototype or `heat` resource exists]

A waste incinerator building can alternatively consume typed waste and produce heat (per spec/waste.md's incinerator_heat coupling), feeding the same district heat network as a coal plant. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, depends on the waste story 'Waste incineration produces power or district heat']

A heat plant supplied with its full recipe input (0.28 coal per tick, 30 workers assigned) produces heat at the recipe's rated output of 350 per tick — the coal-to-heat ratio is a fixed proportional constant, not merely a positive value once inputs are present. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, research/utilities.md §E2 heating_plant_big.ini:3-25]

stories.title: Third pipe network: trunk-and-branch district heating
stories.epic_theme: Heating — district network with temperature-driven demand
stories.i_want: a heat pipe network distinct from water and sewage, with a large-gauge trunk tier and small-gauge branch tier, routed plant to pumping station to endstation to buildings
stories.so_that: heat distribution has real topology and per-km loss like electricity and water

acceptance_criteria.text: Heat pipes form a graph independent of the water and sewage pipe graphs — a building wired for heat is not automatically wired for water. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; ElectricityCache's union-find is a template to clone per-utility, not shared state (docs/egregoria-substrate-audit.md §6)]

Heat delivered at the end of a branch pipe is reduced from the amount injected at the trunk in proportion to pipe length, mirroring the capacity+loss model used for electricity and water. [SUBSTRATE: OURS/ABSENT — greenfield]

A pumping station that is unpowered or unstaffed (offline) delivers no heat past it even when downstream pipe capacity is otherwise available — heat must be actively pumped, so an inoperative pumping station is a distinct failure point, not a passive conduit that merely adds length-loss. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, spec/heating.md:22 $ENGINE_SPEED]

stories.title: Heat demand scales continuously with outdoor temperature
stories.epic_theme: Heating — district network with temperature-driven demand
stories.i_want: a building's heat demand to scale as (20 minus outdoor temperature) times a constant, clamped 0-400%, with no separate winter mode
stories.so_that: cold snaps produce a real, continuous load spike instead of a seasonal flag flip

acceptance_criteria.text: All inhabited and workplace buildings have temperature-driven heat load by default; only explicitly unheated structures (sheds, storage) opt out — inverting W&R's opt-in default to match the cold-climate setting. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield]

stories.title: Unmet district heat falls back to electricity
stories.epic_theme: Heating — district network with temperature-driven demand
stories.i_want: a building short on piped heat to draw extra electricity as an expensive electric-heater fallback, and only go cold if neither pipe heat nor spare electricity is available
stories.so_that: heating failure degrades gracefully instead of jumping straight to an unmet need

acceptance_criteria.text: A building whose heat pipe delivery falls short of its temperature-driven demand draws the shortfall as additional electricity consumption from the building's power connection, provided the electricity network has spare capacity. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, depends on both the heat network and the rebuilt electricity network stories]

A building with neither piped heat nor spare electricity registers its warmth need as unmet, with consequences flowing into the citizen needs/health model rather than a silent no-op. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, depends on spec/needs.md warmth need which is itself unmodelled today]

stories.title: Buildings deposit typed waste into containers
stories.i_want: buildings to fill typed waste containers (mixed, bio, steel, aluminium, plastic, toxic, gravel, burnable, other) rather than an abstract garbage meter
stories.so_that: downstream processing choice (sort vs mixed) has real consequences

acceptance_criteria.text: A residential building deposits waste into a container-stand buffer; the container has per-type sorting bins as an optional planner-built upgrade, and unsorted deposit always goes to a waste_mixed bin. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, zero waste-system footprint in simulation/src]
An industrial recipe building can declare which waste sub-types it emits as production byproducts, distinct from a generic mixed-waste stream. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield]

stories.title: Waste collection reuses the logistics dispatcher
stories.i_want: a full waste container to become a source-job for the same deficit-driven dispatcher that handles ordinary goods logistics, under a WASTE class gate
stories.so_that: there is exactly one dispatch system in the game, not a duplicate garbage-specific one

acceptance_criteria.text: A garbage office building is a fleet-and-fuel dispatch office structurally identical to an ordinary distribution office, differing only in its class gate (WASTE); it does not run its own separate scheduling loop. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; audit could not confirm a generic reusable dispatch-office abstraction exists (FreightStation, souls/freight_station.rs, is a pattern to study, not reuse as-is) — flag any AC assuming a ready-made dispatch office as blocked on the logistics work]

A full waste container is queued as a source-job under the same fleet-limit and class-gate rules as any other logistics source, with no garbage-specific priority formula bypassing the shared dispatcher. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield]

stories.title: Waste processes to recycled material, energy, or landfill
stories.i_want: hauled waste to reach a separation-and-recycling plant (recovers named materials), an incinerator (produces electricity or district heat plus ash), or a landfill (permanent storage), by planner choice
stories.so_that: waste management is a production decision with a real material/energy payoff, not a chore

acceptance_criteria.text: A separation plant consuming waste_mixed produces named material outputs (e.g. gravel, steel, aluminium, plastic) at fixed extraction yields, which re-enter the ordinary item economy as recipe inputs. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield]

An incinerator consuming typed waste produces either electricity — incinerator_powerplant mode converts 3.0 units waste to 33 units electricity — or district heat — incinerator_heat mode converts 2.5 units waste to 450 units heat — plus ash, at fixed per-waste-type burn ratios distinct per mode, with high pollution as a byproduct; the magnitude, not just the presence, of output is fixed by mode. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, cross-couples to the rebuilt electricity network and the heat plant story]

A landfill stores waste permanently — it never empties on its own and has no output — as the residual sink for toxic/unrecyclable material; a demolition/removal action targeting a landfill that still holds waste is rejected. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield]

Waste already sorted into per-type bins at the source routes directly to its type-specific recycling/processing plant, bypassing the separation plant; waste collected as mixed must pass through a separation plant first before any type-specific recycling can consume it. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, spec/waste.md:22]

Toxic waste can alternatively be routed to chemical neutralisation — consuming chemicals and producing high pollution — as a fate distinct from plain landfill storage and from incineration or recycling. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, spec/waste.md:32]

stories.title: Uncollected waste lowers attractiveness and raises sickness
stories.i_want: an overflowing, uncollected container to reduce local attractiveness and raise nearby sickness rate
stories.so_that: neglecting waste collection has a local physical consequence instead of a city-wide meter

acceptance_criteria.text: A container that stays full past its collection threshold for a sustained period reduces the attractiveness score of nearby buildings and raises the local sickness rate, with the effect scoped to the container's vicinity, not applied city-wide. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, depends on an attractiveness/sickness model (spec/healthcare.md) that is itself unmodelled]

stories.title: Cross-border electricity trade via import/export transformers
stories.i_want: dedicated import/export transformer buildings at the border to move electricity in and out as a wired utility link
stories.so_that: cross-border power trade obeys the same physical-causality rule as every other wired connection instead of a magic border toggle

acceptance_criteria.text: An import transformer built at the border injects electricity into the local grid only while it is wire-connected to the local network, drawing from the neighbouring jurisdiction with pricing/currency owned by spec/trade.md; a border tile with no local wire hop imports nothing. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, spec/electricity.md:38-40]

An export transformer sends power across the border only out of the local network's surplus remaining after domestic brownout-priority demand is met — it never creates power that was not first generated locally. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, spec/electricity.md:38-40]

stories.title: Idle consumers still draw baseline lighting power
stories.i_want: a building with no active production to still draw a nonzero idle/lighting electricity load
stories.so_that: pausing production doesn't zero out a building's grid demand

acceptance_criteria.text: A building with no active recipe running still draws a nonzero idleDraw amount of electricity, distinct from and smaller than its full operating consumption. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, spec/electricity.md:32, research/production.md §A4 idleDraw]

stories.title: Grid solver work is budgeted per simulation tick
stories.i_want: the wire-graph solver to amortise a full network resolve across multiple ticks instead of solving the whole grid within one tick
stories.so_that: a large network never causes a single-tick time spike

acceptance_criteria.text: Resolving a large wire network's power flow is spread across multiple simulation ticks (budgeted, amortised) rather than completed within a single tick, mirroring CS1's 256-frame amortisation cycle; the per-tick time spent in the solver stays bounded regardless of network size. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, spec/electricity.md:34-36]

stories.title: Reserve substations from cross-class draw
stories.i_want: to flag a substation as reserved for one consumer class so another class cannot draw from it
stories.so_that: critical residential water supply cannot be crowded out by industrial demand at a shared endstation

acceptance_criteria.text: A substation flagged residential-only rejects draw requests from industrial consumers even when it has spare capacity; industrial demand is routed elsewhere or left unmet rather than drawing from the reserved substation. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, adopted planner policy per spec/water.md:32-34]

stories.title: Derive heat demand from a live outdoor temperature signal
stories.epic_theme: Heating — district network with temperature-driven demand
stories.i_want: a building's heat demand to scale continuously with a live outdoor temperature signal T(t)
stories.so_that: cold snaps produce a real, continuous load spike instead of a seasonal flag flip

acceptance_criteria.text: Building heat demand at outdoor temperature T equals base demand times clamp((20-T) x k, 0, 4). This story is blocked on "Provide a deterministic weather and climate model" landing first — no weather/climate system providing a live T(t) exists anywhere in simulation/src today. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield, no weather or climate system exists in simulation/src (docs/egregoria-substrate-audit.md §6, 'hidden prerequisite'); zero hits for weather|climate|temperature|season across simulation/src]

stories.title: Provide a deterministic weather and climate model
stories.as_a: planner and every system that depends on outdoor conditions
stories.i_want: a temperature signal T(t) with an annual and diurnal cycle that is deterministic, save/load-stable, and updated on an authored cadence
stories.so_that: heat demand and other weather-driven systems have a real, reproducible prerequisite to build on

acceptance_criteria.text: A temperature signal T(t) exists and combines an annual cycle (seasonal swing) with a diurnal cycle (day/night swing) rather than a flat constant or a seasonal flag. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; zero hits for weather|climate|temperature|season across simulation/src]

T(t) is fully deterministic under a fixed seed: the simulation's per-tick state-hash harness produces identical hashes across repeated runs with weather enabled. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; zero hits for weather|climate|temperature|season across simulation/src]

Weather state survives a save/load round-trip: T(t) resumes from the exact point it was saved at, not from a re-seeded or reset clock. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; zero hits for weather|climate|temperature|season across simulation/src]

Weather state updates on an authored cadence (a fixed tick interval), not once at world creation and never again. [SUBSTRATE: ABSENT — greenfield; zero hits for weather|climate|temperature|season across simulation/src]

scenarios.title: Building on a powered road but without a laid wire stays dark
preconditions: A producer with spare capacity exists on the map
A road connects the producer's tile to a building's tile
No wire hop has been placed between the road/producer and the building

steps.action: Advance simulation ticks with the building requesting power
expected: Building reports unpowered
ElectricityCache-style road-adjacency reachability is not consulted for power state

final_observables: Building's power-consuming recipe does not run for lack of electricity input
owning_story_titles: Replace road-adjacency power with laid-wire connectivity

scenarios.title: Deficit subnetwork brownouts industry before housing goes dark
preconditions: One subnetwork with a hospital, a housing block, and an industrial consumer, all wired to the same underpowered producer
Total demand exceeds available supply

steps.action: Reduce plant fuel input so supply falls below total demand
expected: Industrial consumer's draw is reduced (brownout) first
Housing draw reduced only if industry brownout alone doesn't close the deficit
Hospital retains full power longest

final_observables: No consumer goes to full blackout while a lower-priority consumer still has full power

scenarios.title: Food factory rejects sub-threshold quality water
preconditions: A treatment plant delivering water at quality 0.80 to a food-factory recipe building requiring quality >= 0.97
Flow rate is otherwise sufficient

steps.action: Run a tick with the food factory attempting to consume water
expected: Water input is rejected/gated despite sufficient volume
Recipe does not advance for lack of usable water input

final_observables: Factory output remains at pre-tick level; no water quality bypass occurs
owning_story_titles: Water sourced, treated, and piped with a quality grade

scenarios.title: Sewage treatment recovers second-grade water, never food-grade
preconditions: A sewage treatment plant configured per spec (chemicals+power+workers -> water)

steps.action: Run treatment with full chemical/power/worker input
expected: Output water quality is capped at 0.85
Output quality never exceeds fresh treatment's 0.99 ceiling

final_observables: Recovered water cannot satisfy a consumer requiring quality > 0.85 (e.g. a 0.97-threshold food factory)

scenarios.title: Sewage backup with no discharge point gates the producer's tap
preconditions: A producer generating sewage into a local buffer
Its sewage network has no reachable discharge point and treatment is at capacity

steps.action: Continue producing sewage past local buffer capacity
expected: Producer's water consumption is gated (blocked)
No sewage silently disappears

final_observables: Producer's recipe requiring water halts until buffer space frees via eventual treatment capacity
owning_story_titles: Sewage overflow backs up and gates water use

scenarios.title: Cold snap without weather system cannot compute heat demand
preconditions: A building with temperature-driven heat demand wired into the district heat network
No weather/climate system providing T(t) exists yet

steps.action: Attempt to evaluate clamp((20-T) x k, 0, 4) for the building's demand
expected: No valid T(t) is available
Story is blocked pending the weather/climate prerequisite landing

final_observables: Heat demand story cannot be implemented standalone; roadmap must sequence weather/climate first
owning_story_titles: Heat demand scales continuously with outdoor temperature

scenarios.title: Heat shortfall draws extra electricity before a home goes cold
preconditions: A building's heat pipe delivery is below its (mocked/fixed) temperature-driven demand
The building's electricity connection has spare capacity

steps.action: Run a tick with the heat deficit present
expected: Building's electricity draw increases by the heat shortfall amount
Building's warmth need remains satisfied via the electric fallback

final_observables: Building only registers unmet warmth need once electricity is also unavailable
owning_story_titles: Unmet district heat falls back to electricity

scenarios.title: Waste incinerator feeds either the electricity or heat network
preconditions: An incinerator building configured to consume waste_burnable
Wired into either the electricity network or the heat network

steps.action: Run incineration with sufficient waste input
expected: Electricity-mode incinerator converts 3.0 units waste into 33 units electricity onto its wired electricity network
Heat-mode incinerator converts 2.5 units waste into 450 units heat onto its wired heat network
Ash byproduct is produced in both modes

final_observables: Downstream network (electricity or heat) receives the incinerator's output like any other generator
owning_story_titles: Waste processes to recycled material, energy, or landfill
Heat plants burn fuel into district heat

scenarios.title: Full waste container becomes a dispatcher source-job
preconditions: A garbage office with an available truck
A container at or above its collection fill threshold

steps.action: Advance ticks so the dispatcher evaluates jobs
expected: Container is queued as a WASTE-class source-job
A garbage-office truck is dispatched to collect it via the same dispatcher logic as ordinary goods jobs

final_observables: Container fill level drops after truck collection; no separate garbage-only scheduling path was used
owning_story_titles: Waste collection reuses the logistics dispatcher

scenarios.title: Import transformer feeds the local grid across the border
preconditions: An import transformer built at a border tile
The transformer is wire-connected to the local network

steps.action: Advance ticks with local demand exceeding local generation
expected: Import transformer draws power from across the border
Imported power is injected into the local grid like any other producer

final_observables: Local consumers downstream of the import transformer receive power sourced across the border, priced per spec/trade.md
owning_story_titles: Cross-border electricity trade via import/export transformers

scenarios.title: Idle building still draws baseline lighting power
preconditions: A building wired to a powered network with no active recipe running

steps.action: Advance a tick with the building idle
expected: Building's electricity draw equals its idleDraw baseline, not zero
idleDraw is strictly less than the building's full operating draw

final_observables: Network demand accounting includes the idle building's baseline draw
owning_story_titles: Idle consumers still draw baseline lighting power

scenarios.title: Large grid solve stays within its per-tick time budget
preconditions: A wire network large enough that a full resolve cannot complete within one tick's budget

steps.action: Advance ticks while the solver amortises the resolve
expected: No single tick's solver time exceeds the configured per-tick budget
The full network resolve completes across multiple ticks

final_observables: Power state converges to the correct resolved values after the amortised solve finishes, without a single-tick spike
owning_story_titles: Grid solver work is budgeted per simulation tick

scenarios.title: Industrial consumer cannot draw from a residential-reserved substation
preconditions: A substation flagged residential-only with spare capacity
An industrial consumer wired only to that substation

steps.action: Advance a tick with the industrial consumer requesting water
expected: Draw request from the industrial consumer is rejected at the reserved substation
Residential consumers on the same substation are unaffected

final_observables: Industrial consumer's water need goes unmet or is routed to a different, non-reserved substation

scenarios.title: Sorted waste bypasses the separation plant; mixed waste does not
preconditions: One container with per-type sorting bins in use
One container collecting only mixed waste
Both feed the same downstream recycling plants

steps.action: Dispatch collection from both containers to the recycling network
expected: Sorted waste reaches its type-specific recycling plant directly, with no separation-plant hop
Mixed waste is routed through a separation plant before reaching any type-specific recycling plant

final_observables: Sorted waste's recycling throughput is unblocked by separation-plant capacity; mixed waste's is not
owning_story_titles: Waste processes to recycled material, energy, or landfill

scenarios.title: Offline pumping station stops district heat delivery past it
preconditions: A district heat trunk line running through a pumping station to downstream buildings
Downstream pipe capacity is otherwise sufficient

steps.action: Remove power or workers from the pumping station and advance ticks
expected: No heat is delivered past the offline pumping station
Downstream buildings register unmet heat demand despite sufficient pipe capacity

final_observables: Restoring the pumping station's power/workers resumes heat delivery past it
owning_story_titles: Third pipe network: trunk-and-branch district heating

scenarios.title: Consumer classes gate at different water-quality thresholds
preconditions: An animal farm, a food factory, and a nuclear cooling consumer each wired to the same network
Delivered water quality is 0.90 (below food factory's 0.97 and animal farm's 0.93, above nuclear cooling's 0.60)

steps.action: Run a tick with all three consumers attempting to draw water
expected: Food factory rejects the water (0.90 < 0.97)
Animal farm rejects the water (0.90 < 0.93)
Nuclear cooling accepts the water (0.90 >= 0.60)

final_observables: Only the nuclear cooling consumer's recipe advances this tick; the other two remain gated
owning_story_titles: Water sourced, treated, and piped with a quality grade

scenarios.title: Outdoor temperature is reproducible across a save/load round-trip
preconditions: A deterministic TestCtx world with a fixed seed and weather enabled
No other systems need to be active for this scenario

steps.action: Tick the world to an arbitrary point mid-cycle and record T(t)
expected: T(t) is a finite value consistent with the annual/diurnal cycle

steps.action: Save the world, then load it back into a fresh TestCtx
expected: The load succeeds with no error

steps.action: Tick the loaded world by zero ticks and read T(t) again
expected: T(t) immediately after load equals T(t) immediately before save, bit-for-bit

steps.action: Tick both the original (had it kept running) and the loaded world forward by the same number of ticks and compare
expected: The two T(t) trajectories are identical
The per-tick state hash is identical between the two runs

final_observables: T(t) is bit-for-bit reproducible across a save/load round-trip
No nondeterminism is introduced by the weather subsystem
owning_story_titles: Provide a deterministic weather and climate model
